## formal
Let $k$ be $\Q$ or any ordered field and $\Cl_{k}(\ell,\ell)$ the algebra of $\ell$ modes: generators $e_{j}$, $f_{j}$ with $Q(e_{j}) = 1$, $Q(f_{j}) = -1$, mode parities $p_{j} = f_{j}e_{j}$, adjoint $\dagger$ the linear extension of the inverse on blades (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}), scalar part $\langle x\rangle_{0}$. Let $\Gamma = p_{1}\cdots p_{\ell}$ be the total parity, $\alpha(x) = \Gamma x\Gamma$ (the grade involution: it fixes even blades and negates odd ones) and $E = \tfrac12(\mathrm{id} + \alpha)$ the total-parity average (Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} in its total-parity form). A functional $\omega$ is \emph{even} if $\omega \circ \alpha = \omega$. An \emph{observable} is an $a$ with $a^{\dagger} = a$, $a^{2} = 1$; it is \emph{homogeneous} if $\alpha(a) = a$ or $\alpha(a) = -a$. \emph{(P)} is Premise \claimref{synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values}; a \emph{state} is a functional satisfying it. The \emph{record map} of an observable $a$ is
\[
E_{a}(x) = \tfrac12(x + axa) = P_{+}xP_{+} + P_{-}xP_{-}, \qquad P_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm a) .
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The record map; proved.)} $E_{a}$ is linear and idempotent, $E_{a}(1) = 1$, $E_{a}(x^{\dagger}) = E_{a}(x)^{\dagger}$, $E_{a}(xx^{\dagger}) = (P_{+}x)(P_{+}x)^{\dagger} + (P_{-}x)(P_{-}x)^{\dagger}$, and $E_{a}(P_{+}xP_{-}) = 0$. So if $\omega$ satisfies (P) then so does $\omega \circ E_{a}$, and $\omega \circ E_{a}$ vanishes on the elements $P_{+}xP_{-}$ and $P_{-}xP_{+}$ that connect the two sectors of $a$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Records and parity; proved.)} For an observable $a$ the following are equivalent: (1) under (P), $\omega \circ E_{a}$ is even for every even state $\omega$; (2) $E_{a}\alpha = \alpha E_{a}$; (3) $a$ is homogeneous.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(One mode per party, under (P); proved.)} In $\Cl_{k}(2,2)$ with the parties of clause (vii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate} (mode $1$, and mode $2$ twisted by $p_{1}$ as in Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}), the homogeneous observables other than $\pm 1$ are $\pm X_{1}$, $\pm Z_{1}$ for party $1$ and $\pm X_{2}$, $\pm Z_{2}$ for party $2$, where $X_{1} = e_{1}$, $X_{2} = e_{2}p_{1}$ (odd) and $Z_{1} = p_{1}$, $Z_{2} = p_{2}$ (even). For every choice $A_{1}, A_{2}$ among the first four and $B_{1}, B_{2}$ among the second four, with $C = A_{1}(B_{1} + B_{2}) + A_{2}(B_{1} - B_{2})$, $U = X_{1}X_{2}$ and $V = Z_{1}Z_{2}$: $E(C) = \mu U + \nu V$ with $|\mu| + |\nu| \le 2$, and every even state has $|\omega(C)| = |\omega(E(C))| \le 2$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The settings above $2$ are of mixed parity; proved by an example.)} With $B_{1} = \tfrac35X_{2} + \tfrac45Z_{2}$, $B_{2} = \tfrac45X_{2} - \tfrac35Z_{2}$, $A_{1} = X_{1}$, $A_{2} = Z_{1}$, the functional $\omega(x) = \langle(1 + U)(1 + V)x\rangle_{0}$ is an even state and $\omega(C) = \tfrac{14}{5} > 2$. $B_{1}$ is not homogeneous, and $\omega \circ E_{B_{1}}$ is not even: its value on the odd element $X_{1}Z_{2}$ is $\tfrac{12}{25}$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Odd observables with two modes per party, under (P); proved.)} In $\Cl_{k}(4,4)$ let $A_{1} = e_{1}$, $A_{2} = e_{2}$, $B_{1} = e_{3}p_{1}p_{2}$, $B_{2} = e_{4}p_{1}p_{2}$. All four are odd observables, blades up to sign; $A_{i}$ commutes with $B_{j}$; $C$ and $K = -A_{1}A_{2}B_{1}B_{2}$ are even, and the functional $\omega(x) = \langle(1 + K)(1 + \tfrac13C)x\rangle_{0}$ is an even state with $\omega(C) = \tfrac83 > 2$. The record maps of the four observables commute with $\alpha$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued, not part of the theorem).} Premise \claimref{one-relation.recorded-sectors-superselected-premise} says that after a record the recorded sectors do not interfere; for a two-valued observable $a$ and values given by a functional $\omega$, the functional with no interference between the sectors of $a$ and the same values on what commutes with $a$ is $\omega \circ E_{a}$. Premise \claimref{singularity.p-univalence} says that physical states are even. If both hold, before and after a record, then by (ii) an observable that can be recorded is even or odd, never a sum of the two. Odd observables are then allowed, one mode per party gives at most $2$ in both settings, and a value above $2$ needs two modes per party whether the observables are even (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-with-parity-even-observables-needs-two-modes-per-party-and-no-klein-twist}) or odd (clause (v)).

## technical
The univalence premise restricts states to those that vanish on parity-odd elements; it says nothing directly about observables. This result supplies the link through records, under (P), positivity of values, for the statements about states. Reading a record of a two-valued observable $a$ as the map $E_{a}(x) = \tfrac12(x + axa)$, which removes the interference between the two sectors of $a$ and sends states to states, the theorem is: $E_{a}$ sends every even state to an even state exactly when $a$ is even or odd under the total parity. An observable that is a sum of an even and an odd part, such as the direction $\tfrac35e_{1} + \tfrac45p_{1}$ of one mode, turns an even state into one that is not even. In the realisation of the CHSH bound with one mode per party and a Klein twist, the only homogeneous observables are $\pm e_{1}$, $\pm p_{1}$ and their twisted partners, and at these settings every even state gives the CHSH combination a value of at most $2$; the settings that reach $14/5$ on an even state use a direction of mixed parity. Parity-odd observables as such are not excluded: with two modes per party, four odd blades give $8/3$ on an even state. So, under the reading that records act by $E_{a}$ and that states stay even after a record, the two settings recorded side by side (even observables, or odd ones with a twist) both need two modes per party, and the one-mode violation is not available. The reading is argued; the algebra is proved.

## lay
The series has a rule that physical states must look the same when every fermion-like mode changes sign ("even" states), but it had no rule about which quantities can be measured. This result connects the two, assuming (P), the series' assumption that averages are never negative on a quantity times its mirror image. When a two-valued quantity is measured and the result recorded, the state changes in a definite way. The theorem says that this change keeps every even state even exactly when the measured quantity is itself purely even or purely odd; a quantity that mixes the two kinds spoils the rule. For two experimenters with one mode each, the only quantities that pass this test are too few to beat the classical limit of 2 on the standard combination of correlations. Quantities of the odd kind are still allowed, but each experimenter needs two modes to exceed 2. This holds if recording works as described and the rule on states holds after a recording too; those two points are a reading of the series' premises, not something proved here.

## one-liner
In $\Cl_{k}(\ell,\ell)$ under (P), the record map $E_{a}(x) = \tfrac12(x + axa)$ of an observable sends every even state to an even state exactly when $a$ is even or odd; with one twisted mode per party the homogeneous settings give every even state $|\omega(C)| \le 2$, a mixed setting gives $\tfrac{14}{5}$ and its record breaks evenness, and two modes per party with odd observables give $\tfrac83$.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} The properties of the adjoint and of the scalar part used are those of the preliminaries of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate}: $\langle xy\rangle_{0} = \langle yx\rangle_{0}$, $\langle x^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = \langle x\rangle_{0}$, $\langle xx^{\dagger}\rangle_{0}$ is the sum of the squares of the coefficients of $x$ (so it vanishes only for $x = 0$), and the scalar part of a product of two blades is zero unless they are equal up to sign; the blades are a basis (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}). The $p_{j}$ are commuting self-adjoint elements of square $1$; $p_{j}$ anticommutes with $e_{j}$, $f_{j}$ and commutes with the other generators, so $\Gamma$ is self-adjoint of square $1$ and anticommutes with every generator: $\alpha$ is the grade involution, an automorphism commuting with $\dagger$, and $E$ is the projection onto the even part, the group average of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} for the group $\{\mathrm{id}, \alpha\}$. Write $x_{+} = E(x)$ and $x_{-} = x - E(x)$. For a self-adjoint blade $s$, $s^{2} = 1$ and $1 \pm s = \tfrac12(1 \pm s)(1 \pm s)^{\dagger}$, so $x \mapsto \langle(1 \pm s)x\rangle_{0}$ satisfies (P) (as does $\langle x\rangle_{0}$), and it is even when $s$ is even.

\emph{(i).} $P_{\pm}$ are self-adjoint idempotents with $P_{+}P_{-} = 0$, $P_{+} + P_{-} = 1$, $a = P_{+} - P_{-}$; expanding gives $P_{+}xP_{+} + P_{-}xP_{-} = \tfrac12(x + axa)$. The listed properties follow: idempotence from $P_{\pm}P_{\mp} = 0$; $E_{a}(xx^{\dagger}) = \sum_{\pm}P_{\pm}xx^{\dagger}P_{\pm} = \sum_{\pm}(P_{\pm}x)(P_{\pm}x)^{\dagger}$. If $\omega$ satisfies (P) then $\omega(E_{a}(xx^{\dagger})) \ge 0$, $\omega(E_{a}(1)) = 1$ and $\omega(E_{a}(x^{\dagger})) = \omega(E_{a}(x)^{\dagger}) = \omega(E_{a}(x))$.

\emph{(ii).} (3) implies (2): $\alpha(E_{a}(x)) = \tfrac12(\alpha(x) + \alpha(a)\alpha(x)\alpha(a)) = E_{a}(\alpha(x))$ when $\alpha(a) = \pm a$. (2) implies (1): $\omega \circ E_{a} \circ \alpha = \omega \circ \alpha \circ E_{a} = \omega \circ E_{a}$, and $\omega \circ E_{a}$ is a state by (i). (1) implies (3): write $a = a_{+} + a_{-}$; both parts are self-adjoint, and $a^{2} = 1$ gives $a_{+}^{2} + a_{-}^{2} = 1$ and $a_{+}a_{-} + a_{-}a_{+} = 0$. \emph{Step 1.} Let $y$ be odd and self-adjoint and $w = E(E_{a}(y))$, even and self-adjoint. For every even state $\omega$, $\omega(E_{a}(y)) = 0$ by (1), and $\omega(E_{a}(y)) = \omega(w)$ since $\omega$ is even. Taking $\omega = \langle\,\cdot\,\rangle_{0}$ and $\omega = \langle(1 \pm s)\,\cdot\,\rangle_{0}$ for the even self-adjoint blades $s$ gives $\langle w\rangle_{0} = 0$ and $\langle sw\rangle_{0} = 0$; a self-adjoint even element is a combination of the scalar and of even self-adjoint blades (a blade is self-adjoint or anti-self-adjoint), so $w = 0$. \emph{Step 2.} Let $x$ be even and self-adjoint and $z = (E_{a}(x))_{-} = \tfrac12(a_{+}xa_{-} + a_{-}xa_{+})$, odd and self-adjoint. For odd self-adjoint $y$, $\langle zy\rangle_{0} = \langle E_{a}(x)y\rangle_{0} = \langle xE_{a}(y)\rangle_{0} = \langle xw\rangle_{0} = 0$ (the scalar part of an even times an odd element is zero; $\langle E_{a}(x)y\rangle_{0} = \langle xE_{a}(y)\rangle_{0}$ by cyclicity; Step 1). For odd anti-self-adjoint $y$, $\langle zy\rangle_{0} = \langle(zy)^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = -\langle yz\rangle_{0} = -\langle zy\rangle_{0}$, so it is zero. Hence $\langle zz^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} = 0$ and $z = 0$:
\[
a_{+}xa_{-} + a_{-}xa_{+} = 0 \qquad \text{for every even self-adjoint } x . \tag{$*$}
\]
\emph{Step 3.} Put $x = a_{+}$ in $(*)$: $a_{+}^{2}a_{-} + a_{-}a_{+}^{2} = 2a_{-} - 2a_{-}^{3} = 0$, so $a_{-}^{3} = a_{-}$ and $q = a_{-}^{2}$ is a self-adjoint even idempotent commuting with $a_{-}$; it commutes with $a_{+}$ (two anticommutations), and $(a_{+}q)(a_{+}q)^{\dagger} = a_{+}^{2}q = (1 - q)q = 0$, so $a_{+}q = 0$. Thus $a_{+} = a_{+}(1 - q)$, $a_{-} = a_{-}q$, $a_{+}^{2} = 1 - q$, $a_{-}^{2} = q$. \emph{Step 4.} For even $x'$ the element $x = qx'(1 - q) + (1 - q)x'^{\dagger}q$ is even and self-adjoint, and $(*)$ reads $a_{+}(1 - q)x'^{\dagger}q\,a_{-} + a_{-}q\,x'(1 - q)a_{+} = 0$. The first term lies in $(1 - q)\mathcal{A}q$ and the second in $q\mathcal{A}(1 - q)$ (with $\mathcal{A}$ the algebra), so each is zero; multiplying $a_{-}qx'(1 - q)a_{+} = 0$ by $a_{-}$ on the left and $a_{+}$ on the right gives $qx'(1 - q) = 0$, and the adjoint statement gives $(1 - q)x'q = 0$. So $q$ commutes with every even element. \emph{Step 5.} An even element commuting with every even element commutes with every product $g_{i}g_{j}$ of two distinct generators; conjugation by $g_{i}g_{j}$ multiplies a blade by $-1$ exactly when the blade contains one of the two generators and not the other, so only the scalar blade and the top blade survive: $q = c_{0} + c_{1}\Gamma$, and $q^{2} = q$ gives $q \in \{0, 1, \tfrac12(1 \pm \Gamma)\}$. If $q = \tfrac12(1 \pm \Gamma)$ then $a_{-}q = (1 - q)a_{-}$ because $a_{-}$ anticommutes with $\Gamma$, while $a_{-}q = qa_{-}$; multiplying by $q$ gives $qa_{-} = 0$, so $a_{-} = a_{-}^{3} = a_{-}q = qa_{-} = 0$ and then $q = a_{-}^{2} = 0$, a contradiction. So $q = 0$, and $a_{-}a_{-}^{\dagger} = q = 0$ gives $a = a_{+}$; or $q = 1$, and $a_{+}a_{+}^{\dagger} = 1 - q = 0$ gives $a = a_{-}$.

\emph{(iii).} The self-adjoint blades of the algebra of mode $1$ are $1$, $e_{1}$, $e_{1}f_{1} = -p_{1}$ ($f_{1}$ is anti-self-adjoint), so its self-adjoint elements are $t + xe_{1} + zp_{1}$; the square is $t^{2} + x^{2} + z^{2} + 2t(xe_{1} + zp_{1})$, which is $1$ only for $\pm 1$ or $t = 0$, $x^{2} + z^{2} = 1$. The even part is $zp_{1}$ and the odd part $xe_{1}$, so the homogeneous ones are $\pm e_{1}$, $\pm p_{1}$. The twisted mode is the image of mode $2$ under the isomorphism $e_{2} \mapsto e_{2}p_{1}$, $f_{2} \mapsto f_{2}p_{1}$ of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, which preserves $\dagger$, parity and $p_{2}$; so its homogeneous observables are $\pm e_{2}p_{1}$, $\pm p_{2}$. A product $A_{i}B_{j}$ is even exactly when both factors are odd (the product is $\pm U$) or both even ($\pm V$), so $E(C) = \mu U + \nu V$; the check enumerates the $256$ choices and finds $|\mu| + |\nu| \le 2$ in each. $U$, $V$ are commuting self-adjoint elements of square $1$, and for signs $\sigma, \tau$
\[
2 - \sigma U - \tau V = \tfrac12(1 - \sigma U)(1 - \sigma U)^{\dagger} + \tfrac12(1 - \tau V)(1 - \tau V)^{\dagger} ,
\]
so a state has $\omega(\sigma U) \le 1$, $\omega(\tau V) \le 1$ for all signs and $|\omega(\mu U + \nu V)| \le |\mu| + |\nu| \le 2$. For an even $\omega$, $\omega(C) = \omega(E(C))$.

\emph{(iv).} $(1 + U)(1 + V) = \tfrac14\bigl((1 + U)(1 + V)\bigr)\bigl((1 + U)(1 + V)\bigr)^{\dagger}$ is even with scalar part $1$, so $\omega$ is an even state. $E(C) = \tfrac35U + \tfrac45V + \tfrac45U + \tfrac35V = \tfrac75(U + V)$ and $\omega(U) = \omega(V) = 1$, so $\omega(C) = \tfrac{14}{5}$. The value $\tfrac{12}{25}$ of $\omega \circ E_{B_{1}}$ on $X_{1}Z_{2}$ is computed by the check.

\emph{(v).} $p_{1}p_{2}$ is even, self-adjoint, of square $1$, anticommutes with $e_{1}$, $e_{2}$ and commutes with $e_{3}$, $e_{4}$; so $e_{3}p_{1}p_{2}$ and $e_{4}p_{1}p_{2}$ are odd, self-adjoint, of square $1$, anticommute with each other and commute with $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$ (two anticommutations each), by the twist of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} applied to the two modes of party $1$ together. The configuration is one of blades with $A_{1}A_{2} = -A_{2}A_{1}$, $B_{1}B_{2} = -B_{2}B_{1}$, so clause (iv) of the CHSH theorem applies: $C^{2} = 4 + 4K$, $KC = C$, and $\langle(1 + K)(1 + rC)x\rangle_{0}$ satisfies (P) for $8r^{2} \le 1$ with value $8r$ on $C$; at $r = \tfrac13$ the check also verifies $(1 + K)(1 + \tfrac13C) = \tfrac34R^{2}$ with $R = (1 + K)(\tfrac23 + \tfrac16C)$ self-adjoint. $C$ and $K$ are products of an even number of odd elements, so the functional is even. The observables are odd, so their record maps commute with $\alpha$ by (ii).

check_py:
"""synthesis.records-keep-even-states-even-only-for-parity-homogeneous-observables: exact checks.

Cl(l,l) of modes: e_k (square +1, index 2k), f_k (square -1, index 2k+1), p_k = f_k e_k; the dagger sends a blade
to its inverse; alpha is the grade involution (conjugation by the total parity). Record map of an observable a:
E_a(x) = (x + a x a)/2.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations, product

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

ONE = GA.sc(F(1))


def dsign(b, sq):
    g = len(b)
    s = (-1) ** (g * (g - 1) // 2)
    for i in b:
        s *= sq[i]
    return s


def dagger(x, sq):
    return {b: c * dsign(b, sq) for b, c in x.items()}


def clean(x):
    return {b: c for b, c in x.items() if c != 0}


def prod(sq, *xs):
    r = ONE
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, sq)
    return clean(r)


def lin(*terms):
    r = {}
    for c, x in terms:
        r = GA.add(r, GA.scal(F(c), x))
    return clean(r)


def s0(x):
    return x.get((), F(0))


def par(x):
    return clean({b: (c if len(b) % 2 == 0 else -c) for b, c in x.items()})


def even(x):
    return clean({b: c for b, c in x.items() if len(b) % 2 == 0})


def odd(x):
    return clean({b: c for b, c in x.items() if len(b) % 2 == 1})


def modes(m):
    sq = tuple(s for _ in range(m) for s in (1, -1))
    e = [GA.gen(2 * k) for k in range(m)]
    f = [GA.gen(2 * k + 1) for k in range(m)]
    p = [prod(sq, f[k], e[k]) for k in range(m)]
    blades = [ONE] + [{tuple(c): F(1)} for r in range(1, 2 * m + 1) for c in combinations(range(2 * m), r)]
    return sq, e, f, p, blades


def is_obs(x, sq):
    return clean(dagger(x, sq)) == clean(x) and prod(sq, x, x) == ONE


def rec(sq, a, x):
    return lin((F(1, 2), x), (F(1, 2), prod(sq, a, x, a)))


def chsh(sq, a1, a2, b1, b2):
    return lin((1, prod(sq, a1, b1)), (1, prod(sq, a1, b2)), (1, prod(sq, a2, b1)), (-1, prod(sq, a2, b2)))


def check_record_map_commutes_with_parity_exactly_for_homogeneous_observables():
    premise("synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra")
    premise("singularity.descent-parity-average")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate")
    sq, e, f, p, blades = modes(2)
    gam = prod(sq, p[0], p[1])
    assert is_obs(gam, sq) and all(prod(sq, gam, b, gam) == par(b) for b in blades)
    # centre of the even subalgebra: blades commuting with every bivector blade
    biv = [b for b in blades if len(next(iter(b))) == 2]
    central = [next(iter(b)) for b in blades if all(GA.commutes(b, w, sq) for w in biv)]
    assert central == [(), (0, 1, 2, 3)]
    x1, z1, x2, z2 = e[0], p[0], prod(sq, e[1], p[0]), p[1]
    hom = [x1, z1, x2, z2, prod(sq, x1, x2), prod(sq, z1, z2), prod(sq, e[0], f[1]), prod(sq, f[0], e[1])]
    blk = lin((F(1, 2), prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (1, p[1])), p[0])), (F(1, 2), prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (-1, p[1])), e[0])))
    mix = [lin((F(3, 5), x1), (F(4, 5), z1)), lin((F(3, 5), x2), (F(4, 5), z2)), lin((F(5, 13), x1), (F(-12, 13), z1)), blk]
    sa_even = [b for b in blades if len(next(iter(b))) % 2 == 0 and clean(dagger(b, sq)) == b and b != ONE]
    states = [ONE] + [lin((1, ONE), (s, b)) for b in sa_even for s in (1, -1)]
    for rho in states:
        assert rho == ONE or rho == lin((F(1, 2), prod(sq, rho, rho)))  # 1 + s = (1 + s)^2 / 2
    odd_sa = [b for b in blades if len(next(iter(b))) % 2 == 1 and clean(dagger(b, sq)) == b]
    for a in hom + mix:
        assert is_obs(a, sq)
        # positivity and the two sectors
        pp, pm = lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(1, 2), a)), lin((F(1, 2), ONE), (F(-1, 2), a))
        for b in blades[:8]:
            assert rec(sq, a, b) == lin((1, prod(sq, pp, b, pp)), (1, prod(sq, pm, b, pm)))
        homog = par(a) == a or par(a) == GA.neg(a)
        commute = all(par(rec(sq, a, b)) == rec(sq, a, par(b)) for b in blades)
        keeps = all(s0(prod(sq, rho, rec(sq, a, y))) == 0 for rho in states for y in odd_sa)
        assert homog == commute == keeps
        assert homog == (a in hom)
    # one witness spelled out: the even state <(1 + p1)(1 + p2) x>_0 after a record of (3/5) X1 + (4/5) Z1
    rho = prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (1, p[0])), lin((1, ONE), (1, p[1])))
    assert par(rho) == rho and s0(prod(sq, rho, rec(sq, mix[0], e[0]))) == F(12, 25)
    return True


def check_one_mode_per_party_at_homogeneous_settings_even_states_give_at_most_two():
    premise("tower.commuting-copies")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate")
    sq, e, f, p, blades = modes(2)
    x1, z1, x2, z2 = e[0], p[0], prod(sq, e[1], p[0]), p[1]
    u, v = prod(sq, x1, x2), prod(sq, z1, z2)
    # self-adjoint blades of the two party algebras
    sa1 = [b for b in blades if set(next(iter(b))) <= {0, 1} and clean(dagger(b, sq)) == b]
    assert [next(iter(b)) for b in sa1] == [(), (0,), (0, 1)]
    setsa = [GA.scal(F(s), o) for o in (x1, z1) for s in (1, -1)]
    setsb = [GA.scal(F(s), o) for o in (x2, z2) for s in (1, -1)]
    worst = F(0)
    for a1, a2, b1, b2 in product(setsa, setsa, setsb, setsb):
        ec = even(chsh(sq, a1, a2, b1, b2))
        assert set(ec) <= {next(iter(u)), next(iter(v))}
        tot = sum(abs(c) for c in ec.values())
        assert tot <= 2
        worst = max(worst, tot)
    assert worst == 2
    for su, sv in product((1, -1), repeat=2):
        lhs = lin((2, ONE), (-su, u), (-sv, v))
        rhs = lin((F(1, 2), prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (-su, u)), lin((1, ONE), (-su, u)))),
                  (F(1, 2), prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (-sv, v)), lin((1, ONE), (-sv, v)))))
        assert lhs == rhs
    # contrast: a mixed setting of party 2, an even state, value 14/5, and the record that breaks evenness
    b1 = lin((F(3, 5), x2), (F(4, 5), z2))
    b2 = lin((F(4, 5), x2), (F(-3, 5), z2))
    assert is_obs(b1, sq) and is_obs(b2, sq)
    c = chsh(sq, x1, z1, b1, b2)
    rho = prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (1, u)), lin((1, ONE), (1, v)))
    assert par(rho) == rho and rho == clean(GA.scal(F(1, 4), prod(sq, rho, rho))) and s0(rho) == 1
    assert s0(prod(sq, rho, c)) == F(14, 5) and even(c) == lin((F(7, 5), u), (F(7, 5), v))
    y = prod(sq, x1, z2)
    assert odd(y) == y and s0(prod(sq, rho, y)) == 0
    assert s0(prod(sq, rho, rec(sq, b1, y))) == F(12, 25)
    return True


def check_two_modes_per_party_odd_homogeneous_observables_exceed_two_on_an_even_state():
    premise("tower.commuting-copies")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate")
    sq, e, f, p, blades = modes(4)
    g = prod(sq, p[0], p[1])
    a = (e[0], e[1])
    b = (prod(sq, e[2], g), prod(sq, e[3], g))
    for o in a + b:
        assert is_obs(o, sq) and par(o) == GA.neg(o) and len(o) == 1
    assert all(GA.commutes(x, y, sq) for x in a for y in b)
    assert GA.anticommutes(a[0], a[1], sq) and GA.anticommutes(b[0], b[1], sq)
    c = chsh(sq, *a, *b)
    k = GA.neg(prod(sq, a[0], a[1], b[0], b[1]))
    assert par(c) == c and par(k) == k and is_obs(k, sq)
    assert prod(sq, c, c) == lin((4, ONE), (4, k)) and prod(sq, k, c) == c
    r = F(1, 3)
    rho = prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (1, k)), lin((1, ONE), (r, c)))
    assert par(rho) == rho and s0(rho) == 1 and s0(prod(sq, rho, c)) == F(8, 3) and 8 * r * r <= 1
    # rho is a positive multiple of the square of a self-adjoint element, so its functional satisfies (P)
    s, t = F(2, 3), F(1, 6)
    root = prod(sq, lin((1, ONE), (1, k)), lin((s, ONE), (t, c)))
    assert clean(dagger(root, sq)) == root
    assert prod(sq, root, root) == clean(GA.scal(F(4, 3), rho))
    # records of the four observables commute with the parity (all 256 blades)
    for o in a + b:
        assert all(par(rec(sq, o, y)) == rec(sq, o, par(y)) for y in blades)
    return True
